items.summary: A fast-growing AI-native SaaS team we worked with alongside Supabase was writing 1.8 TB of WAL a day. That number alone made the database look like the ceiling. When we broke it down, about 39% of that WAL was full-page-image overhead. It didn’t come from the application, the platform or the workload. It came from a five-minute checkpoint default. This post walks through why that happens, how to check whether it’s happening to you, and what to do about it. Everything here applies to PostgreSQL on Supabase and on any other platform. items.summary: Every now and then, a PostgreSQL database needs changes: adding a column, creating an index, updating data, or modifying constraints. Changes like these are called migrations. They can finish in seconds and go unnoticed, or lead to blocking, replication lag, unexpected load, or even downtime. Of course, no checklist can guarantee a trouble-free migration. However, asking the right questions beforehand can significantly reduce the risk . In this article, we’ll go through a checklist that can help prepare for PostgreSQL migrations more confidently: What will PostgreSQL actually do? Which lock will it take? Is the database ready?
